children: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD, Financials), the chipmaker that competes with Nvidia in gaming graphics and AI processors, could have a rare opening in the GPU market next year.

Hardware leaker Kepler_L2 has a rumor that AMD is working on a next-gen gaming GPU for the year 2027 that would be the successor of the RX 9070 XT. The same reports also imply that Nvidia might not release its next-gen RTX portfolio until 2028.
If that scheduling holds true, AMD may put a new generation of gaming hardware on the market during the time its major rival is between product cycles.
That's notable because Nvidia is still way ahead of the pack in gaming GPUs. In the August 2026 poll of Steam hardware, Nvidia had 72.88% of users to AMD's 18.68%.
AMD is also said to not have its whole next-gen lineup ready till 2027. Rumors say the flagship GPU and others could launch in 2028, limiting the possible edge.

But even a short-term gap might give AMD a shot among gamers eyeing newer gear, especially if cost and availability cooperate. The corporation is also grappling with increased component costs, and separate sources indicate it might raise GPU and CPU prices.

Wall Street is positive with TipRanks showing 29 Buy ratings and six Holds with an average price target of $644.62. Now the question is whether AMD can leverage a possible one-year product lead into enduring market-share gains.

title: AMD stock rises on a rumor that could give it a 2027 GPU edge
